breaking.title: RBI Restores 90% Daily CRR Requirement From 1 Dec Amid Liquidity Tightening
breaking.summary: RBI reduces banks' daily CRR maintenance requirement from 99% to 90% from December 1, releasing Rs 50,000 crore amid tight liquidity. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to reduce the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for banks from 99 per cent to 90 per cent, effective 1 December 2026, as liquidity conditions in the banking system tighten and short-term interest rates rise. The move is expected to release around Rs 50,000 crore into the banking system, providing banks with additional liquidity at a time when the system has moved into a deficit.

breaking.title: RBI Clubs 25 Card Payment Circulars Into A Single Framework
breaking.summary: The RBI has clubbed 25 existing circulars, governing debit, credit and prepaid card transactions, under a single regulatory framework. Called the Reserve Bank of India (Digital Payments – Card-based transaction) Directions, 2026 , the new norms look to streamline compliance and security rules for card-based digital payments. The new rules also replace the need for referring multiple instructions issued over the years. The new framework, which comes into force with immediate effect, primarily pertains to banks, non-bank payment system providers, and ecosystem participants under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.

breaking.title: SEBI Allows FPIs in Physically Settled Commodity Derivatives from June 2027
breaking.summary: SEBI permits FPIs to trade in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives from June 1, 2027, subject to prescribed risk safeguards. Summary : The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), through Circular HO/47/16/13(17)2026-MRD-POD1/I/26650/2026 dated November 27, 2026, permits Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts , excluding options in goods, with effect from June 1, 2027. The circular revises the August 4, 2023 Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives Segment to deepen institutional participation and liquidity. FPIs must unwind or roll over positions before the tender or staggered delivery period.
